units.explanation: The bounded native model download consumes the streamed response; not every workspace futures consumer.
Native model downloads/probes and always-compiled private handoff/setup origin validation use reqwest::Url. Setup parsing does not send an outbound request; it adds no new crate owner.
Native model IPC, nested fields and auth/handoff/setup protocols share serde derives; optional listeners serialize the corresponding bridge profiles.

Strict handoff/setup envelope JSON, model manifests and local auth candidate serialization share serde_json. The setup catalog remains an opaque bounded value here; complete catalog validation belongs to the frontend.
Handoff proofs, model integrity and setup catalog/envelope/challenge digests share SHA-256. These production owner edges remain production context when host tests exercise them.

Proof decoding, model checksum encoding, optional inference identity decoding and random transport IDs use the same hex edge; the setup listener adds an ID encoding call only when local-app-handoff is enabled.

Feature-owned Tauri IPC commands, main-window checks, managed auth/handoff/setup state, asset resolution, native runtime and nested errors retain the same owner. Unrelated core command behavior is not audited.
Native model download/DNS/synchronization, optional inference spawn_blocking and feature-gated auth/handoff/setup listener operations retain the Tokio owner.
The model selection resource probe reads available RAM and disk via this direct owner.
Optional host inference compile coverage only; not enabled by either all-WebGPU APK profile.

The exact optional sys 0.1.150 constraint preserves the wrapper 0.1.150 native ABI. It adds no sys default features and is activated only by the four existing host inference profiles, not Android or default tests. This is a manifest compatibility edge, not a new direct FFI call.
Optional native inference renders model-supplied Jinja templates; this runtime is not in the local Android all-WebGPU builds.
Optional host model-template compatibility; preserve its exact direct owner, separate from Android WebGPU.

The shared Result returned by the native URL/IPC bridge contains this derived error schema; all nested external error types are retained. The upstream merge deliberately resolves thiserror 2.0.18 rather than 2.0.19 because PocketIC 16.0.0 requires the exact 2.0.18 version. The unchanged native workspace dependency accepts version 2; the checksum-verified cached 2.0.18 archive retains MIT OR Apache-2.0 and pins thiserror-impl exactly to 2.0.18. This updates the existing production owner identity, not the feature boundary or a new backend audit root. Cargo metadata, native build and advisory qualification remain separate.
Nested shared native error variant is part of the bridge Result even on hosts; it is not omitted because its media call sites are outside the feature boundary.
Native bundle serving determines cache MIME; this helper is compiled with the plugin. The local APK rejects OTA caches via bundled policy.
Source-owned native bundled/cache compatibility gate keeps the local client from selecting an old live-production bundle. No legacy OTA downloader or unrelated backend root is added.
The native build hook generates permissions for model commands and auth/handoff/setup bridges for each selected plugin profile; setup adds command names, not an external build dependency.
The selected open-chat shell instantiates the native plugin and bundled-window navigation. Core notification/deep-link behavior is not a new feature-owned root.
Builds the current shell assets and local-test capabilities; not executed by plugin-only default host library tests.

Workspace versions and exact feature forwarding are bound, not whole-workspace audit roots. No new target-specific Cargo declarations are added. The optional direct sys ABI constraint is covered by plugin.native.inference-sys. Both APK profiles retain all-WebGPU and private-app handoff (also gating setup), but the app no longer forwards local-test-browser-auth. The dormant plugin local-browser-auth declaration is not selected. Host commands remain separate nonshipping checks.

Reviewed native dispatch, commands, errors and model nested structs. The unchanged browser-auth protocol remains compiled and its listener remains dormant source behind unselected local-browser-auth; it is not the APK sign-in path. Original Credential Manager auth/session restoration is reviewed in its frontend/JVM boundaries, not a new Rust credential store. Always-compiled handoff validation now accepts only the exact client-encrypted envelope and rejects plaintext payload/recipient fields, malformed encodings and wrong bounds with existing serde/JSON/reqwest/SHA owners and standard-library validation; Rust never decrypts its fields. Setup validates a bounded opaque catalog envelope with those same owners; full catalog/package/processor/origin validation remains frontend responsibility. Optional inference retains llama-cpp-2/minijinja/minijinja-contrib plus the reviewed exact sys ABI constraint. Embedded tests add no separate dev dependencies or downgraded production edges.

The selected handoff/setup listeners retain bytes/getrandom/http-body-util/hyper/hyper-util, serde/JSON/hex/Tokio and standard-library owners. Setup shares the local-app-handoff gate and transports a bounded opaque catalog, not drafts or credentials. The retained browser-auth listener source uses the same owners but is unselected in every reviewed profile. The two APK profiles and two explicit nonshipping host listener-test profiles enable handoff/setup listeners. Default and inference host checks still do not. The retained server tasks cancel authority on platform loss, drain bounded terminal HTTP responses and release the owner without a further UI poll. Host listener tests with a fake retention backend do not qualify the Android foreground service or installed APK.

Current shell entry/navigation uses Tauri and the local oc plugin only at the changed feature boundary. Standard-library main calls app_lib; local-test capability JSON adds no Rust external owner. Existing unrelated notification/deep-link/media/update-download implementation and disabled devtools telemetry are outside the feature-owned roots, not claimed as audited. The bundled cache gate retains tauri, serde/JSON, semver and mime_guess owners; zip is only the unchanged legacy OTA downloader, not the selected local APK policy-none path. Local handoff/setup capabilities remain restricted to the bundled main window; browser-auth capability is absent. The builder requires the original Credential Manager marker and handoff/setup assets while rejecting browser-auth HTML/JS assets. Its imported profile helper selects the original RP identifier and account-linking UI without granting or asserting provider/Digital Asset Links authorization. These build inputs add no Rust dependency owner.

The feature-gated RetentionLease uses only std Arc/atomic synchronization and a payload-free RetentionBackend trait. Bounded startup is acknowledged before returning a relay URL; failure releases the owner, only the existing authenticated handoff claim can extend retention, loss fails closed, and release/drop is idempotent. Listener drain/terminal cleanup uses the already-reviewed Tokio and HTTP owners. Android-only mobile dispatch serializes owner/deadline metadata through existing serde/JSON/Tauri, never draft fields or credentials. Linux/Windows feature tests exercise actual Rust listener and lease code with an in-process test backend, not Android service/provider behavior. The Kotlin foreground-service overlay and Android dependencies have their own scoped inventory; this unit adds no Cargo dependency, feature declaration, advisory decision or runtime acceptance.
